name: Corbitt Manufacturing Company
old_description: Since 1948 we have supported the transportation, construction, industrial tool, farm and foodservice industries. We deliver the top-quality products you need, when and where you need it. Guaranteed.
about:
Corbitt Manufacturing Company operates from a 100,000-square-foot facility in Paragould, Arkansas. Founded in 1948, the business began as a diversified contract manufacturer specializing in permanent-mold aluminum castings, machined components, custom tooling, and complete assemblies. In 2019, the company was acquired by The Greenbrier Companies and now operates as a Greenbrier subsidiary.

The plant houses three CNC machining centers and three furnaces feeding multiple pour lines, supported by grinders, broaching machines, milling machines, lathes, and a range of presses including a Dake 375-ton hydraulic press, a Bliss SC2 500-ton press, and a Niagara HBM 175-ton press. Standard permanent-mold castings run up to 75 pounds with a maximum mold envelope of 48 by 62 inches, while machining services cover prototype design, reverse engineering, wire and RAM EDM, gear cutting, jig and fixture building, and assembly. Production volumes span from one-off prototypes to several hundred thousand units annually.

Corbitt serves OEMs in earth-moving, mining, agricultural, electrical, transportation, recreation, and food-service markets. In transportation it produces dock cleats, transmission casings, manifolds, and railroad-car parts as the industry shifts from iron to aluminum. For food service it re-engineered a motor housing that eliminated leakage and cut scrap rates. Electrical work includes explosion-proof receptacles and power-line connectors, while powertrain projects focus on light- and heavy-duty gearboxes held to super-close tolerances.

The company emphasizes a "what you need, when and where you need it" delivery guarantee backed by in-house testing protocols that fast-track part deployment. Engineering staff provide troubleshooting expertise on every project, positioning Corbitt as a problem-solving partner rather than a pure production shop.
